facts.statement: The genus Parvodus was named by Rees and Underwood in 2001.
facts.quote: authority: Rees & Underwood, 2001

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Parvodus is Lissodus rugianus.
facts.quote: type_species: Lissodus rugianus

facts.statement: The type species Lissodus rugianus was originally described by Ansorge in 1990.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Ansorge, 1990

facts.statement: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont sharks that lived during the Mesozoic era.
facts.quote: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont, known from the Mesozoic era.

facts.statement: Parvodus belongs to the parent group Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lonchidiidae

facts.statement: Parvodus is classified within the family Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Family: Lonchidiidae

facts.statement: Parvodus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
facts.quote: Class: Chondrichthyes

facts.statement: There are 81 recorded fossil occurrences of Parvodus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 81

facts.statement: The species P. curvidens was described by Duffin and Thies in 1997 from Kimmeridgian deposits in Germany.
facts.quote: P. curvidens (Duffin and Thies, 1997), Kimmeridgian, Germany

facts.statement: The species P. ominechonensis was described by Breeden et al. in 2024 from Carnian deposits in Japan.
facts.quote: P. ominechonensis Breeden et al., 2024, Carnian, Japan

facts.statement: The species P. pattersoni was described by Duffin in 1985 from Bathonian deposits in England and Scotland.
facts.quote: P. pattersoni (Duffin, 1985), Bathonian, England and Scotland

facts.statement: The species P. rugianus was described by Ansorge in 1990 from Berriasian-Valanginian deposits in England, Germany, Denmark, and Sweden.
facts.quote: P. rugianus (Ansorge, 1990) Berriasian-Valanginian, England, Germany, Denmark and Sweden

facts.statement: The species P. graciliani was described by Ribeiro and França in 2026 from Tithonian deposits in Brazil.
facts.quote: P. graciliani Ribeiro & França, 2026, Tithonian, Brazil.

facts.statement: The species P. graciliani was named in 2026 to honor the Brazilian writer Graciliano Ramos.
facts.quote: In 2026, a new species of Parvodus was published: P. graciliani, honoring the Brazilian writer Graciliano Ramos (1892–1953), author of the novel Vidas Secas.

facts.statement: The species P. graciliani is known from isolated teeth found in lacustrine deposits of the Aliança Formation in the Jatobá Basin.
facts.quote: This new species was described based on isolated teeth recovered from lacustrine deposits of the Aliança Formation in the Jatobá Basin

facts.statement: A 2023 paper assigned the species P. huizodus, from the Early Triassic of China, to the genus Parvodus.
facts.quote: A 2023 paper assigned the newly described species P. huizodus from the Early Triassic of China to the genus.

facts.statement: The species P. celsucuspus was reported from the Early Cretaceous of England and France.
facts.quote: The species Parvodus celsucuspus Rees et al., 2013 has been reported from the Early Cretaceous of England and France.

facts.statement: A single tooth of Parvodus sp. has been reported from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) of France.
facts.quote: A single tooth of Parvodus sp. has also been reported from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) of France.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the species P. heterodon belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be placed in the genus Polyacrodus.
facts.quote: Some later studies also included the species Parvodus heterodon (Patterson, 1966) from the Early Cretaceous of England in the genus, though other studies have included this species in the genus Polyacrodus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the species "Hybodus" parvidens belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be assigned to the genus Polyacrodus.
facts.quote: Some studies have also included the species "Hybodus" parvidens Woodward, 1916, from the Early Cretaceous of Europe and North America within Parvodus, though again this species has also been assigned to Polyacrodus.
